Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: Perceived depression scores improved significantly more in the TRI 360TM multi-ingredient supplement group than in the placebo group.
Sentence: "All assessed perception scorings on psychological symptoms like fatigue, mental stress, sleep disturbance, anxiety, depression, emotional trauma, mood changes, self-confidence, willpower, and motivation were very significantly (p ≤ 0.0001) improved in TRI 360TM participants than placebo control group."
Measured as: depression perception scoring
Population: Adults aged 20-45 years with one or more psychological symptoms
Intervention: TRI 360TM proprietary nutraceutical combination capsules twice a day, up to 180 days
Comparator: Placebo
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 84
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: no effect
Claim: No consistent interaction between vitamin D treatment and baseline CRP on depressive symptoms across outcomes.
Sentence: "No consistent interaction between treatment and baseline CRP was observed across outcomes."
Measured as: depressive symptoms (BDI-II, DISYPS, self- and proxy-rated)
Population: Depressed, vitamin D-deficient adolescents (25(OH)D ≤ 30 nmol/l, BDI-II ≥ 14)
Intervention: Vitamin D 2640 IU/day for 28 days plus treatment as usual
Comparator: Placebo plus treatment as usual
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 92
baseline_vitamin_d_status: below_20_ng_ml

{
  "rationale": "The conflict is apparent because Study A measured perceived depression as one item on a broad symptom checklist, whereas Study B tested a treatment-by-CRP interaction on full depression scales (BDI-II, DISYPS).",
